s: After a currency depreciation, the J-curve effect implies that the trade balance generally:
o: Worsens only when exports become cheaper abroad
Remains unchanged because prices do not change
Improves immediately and then worsens permanently
First worsens and improves only after export and import volumes adjust
x: Under the J-curve effect, import bills rise immediately after depreciation, so the trade balance initially worsens; it improves later as quantities adjust.
tq: Apply the time sequence—initial price effect followed by volume adjustment—to the trade balance.
sec: Exchange rate and trade - devaluation, J-curve, Marshall-Lerner

s: Which of the following correctly describes the immediate effects of devaluation or depreciation?
o: Exports become cheaper abroad and imports become dearer at home
Exports become dearer abroad and imports become cheaper at home
Both exports and imports become cheaper at home
Neither export nor import prices are affected
x: Devaluation or depreciation makes domestic exports cheaper for foreign buyers and imports more expensive in the domestic market.
tq: Track the direction of price changes separately in foreign and domestic markets.
sec: Exchange rate and trade - devaluation, J-curve, Marshall-Lerner

s: According to the Marshall–Lerner condition, devaluation improves the trade balance when:
o: Only export demand is perfectly inelastic
The sum of export and import demand price elasticities is greater than one
The sum of export and import demand price elasticities is equal to zero
The sum of export and import demand price elasticities is less than one
x: The Marshall–Lerner condition is satisfied when the sum of the absolute values of export and import demand price elasticities exceeds one.
tq: Recall the threshold condition and distinguish greater than one from less than one.
sec: Exchange rate and trade - devaluation, J-curve, Marshall-Lerner

s:

Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the immediate rise in import bills explains the initial worsening described by the J-curve effect.
tq: Test whether the reason explains the time-order mechanism in the assertion.
